newsitem.title: INDIA: India eases norms for non-government pension funds.
newsitem.headline: India eases norms for non-government pension funds.

text.p: The Indian government on Monday relaxed investment pattern norms by non-government employees' provident funds, a Finance Ministry statement said.
Finance Minister P. Chidambaram had in the 1997/98 (April-March) federal budget had announced that the government would relax norms of investment for provident funds.
The funds were so far required to deposit 20 percent of fresh additions to their corpus in a special deposit scheme.

They will now be free to invest the 20 percent incremental funds in securities issued or guaranteed by the federal for state government or in securities of state-owned firms and financial institutions, the statement said.
The new norms of investment for non-government provident funds will be applicable from April 1, it added.
